name: Youth of Today
label: Revelation
lede: Ray Cappo and John Porcelly left a Danbury hardcore band, picked the plainest name available, and aimed it at New York. Put an X on it, skip the beer, skip the burger, mean every word: a whole scene copied the dress code.

eras.title: Danbury kids, plain name
eras.text: Ray Cappo and John Porcelly came out of Violent Children, a Danbury, Connecticut hardcore band, and started something blunter. The name was generic, the pitch was a sober, clean-living straight edge message no one had asked for yet, and the target was New York.

years.h: Ray Cappo and John Porcelly pick the most generic name they can find
years.p: They leave Violent Children with Graham Phillips on bass and Darren Pesce on drums. Porcelly later explained the name: "We wanted a generic name because we wanted people to know that we were there to play hardcore."

years.h: Youth of Today play their first show at the Anthrax
years.p: The Connecticut club is the region's hardcore clubhouse. Porcelly credits [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]]'s [[Roger Miret|ab51d57f-5007-4ee4-8461-a4050f8d939d]] and [[Vinnie Stigma|ebc05559-b4e0-4080-87d7-1c6672451491]] with getting them the gig.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ray Cappo · Revelation Records: Youth of Today · Wikipedia: Revelation Records
years.h: Kevin Seconds of 7 Seconds puts out Can't Close My Eyes
years.p: Positive Force No. 4, a 7" on [[Kevin Seconds|dfa1dec9-a570-4a1c-a2bb-0f07f6dbb81b]]'s Reno label, is a straight edge stamp of approval before New York knew the band. The same year Youth of Today land on the Connecticut Fun compilation LP.
years.xp:
Kevin Seconds was a direct influence on Ray Cappo, and Positive Force was the obvious home: the label had built its name on positive, drug-free hardcore. Graham Phillips and Darren Pesce left soon after Can't Close My Eyes, the first of many exits.

The EP never really went away. Revelation later ran a limited fourth pressing, and in 1997 gave it a full reissue.

eras.title: Four drummers and a van
eras.text: Drummers came and went, but Break Down the Walls and a 1987 US tour made Youth of Today the band every kid in a hooded sweatshirt wanted to be. By the end of 1987 there was a label built partly around them, Revelation Records, and a name for the scene: youth crew.

years.h: Craig Setari and Richie Birkenhead fill out the band
years.p: [[Craig Setari|3908d895-a1af-42a7-b86b-93a3074057ee]] comes over from [[Straight Ahead|1fd60d7c-dc35-44f5-9162-4113b6ca4a69]] on bass, and [[Richie Birkenhead|7a1a6273-c31b-4828-8e20-0d6ea66943aa]] joins on second guitar. The drum stool stays up for grabs.

years.h: Drew Thomas and Kevin Seconds take turns behind the kit
years.p: Per Wikipedia, the 1986 drummers run from Darren Pesce to Tommy Carroll, [[Drew Thomas|ebc66701-0d59-49c9-ae21-4937edb96a6a]] of [[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]] and [[Kevin Seconds|dfa1dec9-a570-4a1c-a2bb-0f07f6dbb81b]]. In 1987 Lukey Luke briefly plays bass before Walter Schreifels takes over.

years.h: Break Down the Walls is cut in two days, and Cappo passes out
years.p: On Wishing Well, the California label run out of the [[Uniform Choice|d514a452-7088-4d49-a03c-9e37d76d38ea]] camp, it becomes the youth crew blueprint: fast, chanted, aimed at the kids in the room.
years.xp: Porcelly told No Echo how the vocals went: "Ray was pushing his voice so hard that he actually knocked himself out!" The whole record took two days.

years.h: Revelation Records opens in New Haven to release one record
years.p: Jordan Cooper and Cappo start the label for [[Warzone|496da466-68e9-4cbb-9e86-cbb57eda861a]]'s Lower East Side Crew 7". Cappo steps away from the business in 1988.

years.h: Youth of Today lead off New York City Hardcore: Together
years.p: Revelation's 7" roll call of the new straight edge New York bands, with Youth of Today up first.

q: We thought straight edge was an important message.
yt: Live at the 9:30 Club, Washington, September 9, 1987
years.h: Youth of Today hit the road behind Break Down the Walls
years.p: The five-piece is Cappo, Porcelly, Birkenhead, [[Walter Schreifels|9f350578-acdd-480e-8273-5eaf88842f1c]] on bass and [[Mike Ferraro|edffc714-f0a2-4d6c-b4c0-dc31e713481c]] on drums. Ferraro met Cappo near St. Marks Place and played his first show in Canada with 7 Seconds.
years.xp:
Ferraro learned the set at Giant Studios, and the tour turned into a rolling argument with the old punk world. In Detroit, he told Red Bull Music Academy: "They were throwing fucking deer meat at us. I guess they were doing it because of Ray's vegetarian thing." In Chandler, Arizona, a Nazi skinhead gang called the band out to fight behind a McDonald's, then never turned up.

It was also a conversion drive. Buffalo produced its own disciples in Zero Tolerance, and by the second trip through Southern California the straight edge kids were packing rooms past capacity.

years.h: Sammy Siegler, a teenager from Side By Side, takes the drum stool
years.p: [[Richie Birkenhead|7a1a6273-c31b-4828-8e20-0d6ea66943aa]] leaves to focus on [[Underdog|de38fbd3-7155-497a-bf3c-1a8db3091859]]. [[Sammy Siegler|869c662b-574c-46ac-acf6-3dc6f025fd5a]] replaces Ferraro behind the kit.

eras.title: A trip to India, a heavier record
eras.text: The peak year of youth crew nearly ended Youth of Today. Cappo went to India, came back, and the band made We're Not in This Alone, its heaviest and most pointed record. Straight edge was the floor now, and vegetarianism was the new line.

years.src: Wikipedia: We're Not in This Alone · Wikipedia: Ray Cappo
years.h: Cappo flies to India and the band goes quiet
years.p: Wikipedia records only a brief breakup in 1988. The pull was Krishna consciousness, which Cappo had been following.
years.xp:
Krishna consciousness lined up with everything Youth of Today already preached: no drugs, no drink, no meat. For Ray Cappo it was the next step, not a detour, and it shaped everything he did after the band.

The pause didn't last. Cappo came back to a Youth of Today rebuilt around Walter Schreifels on bass and Sammy Siegler on drums.

yt: Live at City Gardens, Trenton, March 20, 1988
years.h: Revelation reissues Break Down the Walls as REV 8
years.p: The label Cappo co-founded also puts the band on New York City Hardcore: The Way It Is.

years.src: Wikipedia: We're Not in This Alone · Red Bull Music Academy Daily
yt: The No More video, filmed at the Anthrax
years.h: Caroline Records puts out We're Not in This Alone
years.p: Produced by Cappo and Porcelly at Chung King House of Metal in New York, the album opens with Cappo announcing Youth of Today is back.
years.xp:
No More is about the meat industry, and its low-budget video cut in slaughterhouse footage from PETA. It's the moment vegetarianism joins the youth crew uniform. Porcelly told Red Bull Music Academy what the tour for it looked like: "there was a whole subgenre of hardcore now that was straight edge and it was big."

Caroline's original mix came out muddy. Fans complained, and the label remixed and re-pressed it with a REMIX sticker on the sleeve. Live Free started life as an unreleased Project X song.

years.h: Mike Ferraro starts Judge, with Porcelly on riffs
years.p: Ferraro, the 1987 tour drummer, begins Judge as a side project, and Porcelly writes the riffs.
years.xp:
Ferraro, who goes by Mike Judge in the interview, told Red Bull Music Academy how fast it came together: "A week later, I came up with the name Judge and asked Porcell if he was interested in helping out."

His summary of the band's life: "We never stopped until Judge broke up in 1990."

eras.title: One last record, then everyone scatters
eras.text: Youth of Today took the message across Europe in 1989, Yugoslavia included, where there was barely a hardcore circuit to play. Then the band decided it had said what it had to say, put out a farewell 7" on Revelation, and split into Shelter, Judge, Gorilla Biscuits and Quicksand.

years.cap: Youth of Today at Fender's Ballroom, Long Beach, August 1989
years.h: Twelve countries in one run, Yugoslavia included
years.p: Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Yugoslavia, Italy, France, Belgium, the Netherlands and England. A Youth of Today show at Amsterdam's Van Hall later surfaces as a live 7".

years.cap: Youth of Today at Fender's Ballroom, Long Beach, August 1989
q: Straight edge kids were hated back then.
years.src: Wikipedia: Youth of Today · No Echo
years.h: Four songs for Revelation, then Youth of Today are done
years.p: Three of the four also come out as the Disengage single.

years.h: Cappo forms [[Shelter|d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db]] and puts Krishna consciousness up front
years.p: The new band is openly devotional Krishna-core, and Porcelly eventually joins. Schreifels already has [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]] and is headed for [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]].

eras.title: The door never quite shuts
eras.text: There was never one big reunion. Youth of Today kept leaving the door open: short runs of shows, a remixed We're Not in This Alone, and new kids finding the name while Cappo's Shelter carried on.

years.h: The We're Not in This Alone line-up plays again
years.p: Cappo, Porcelly, Schreifels and Siegler briefly reunite.

years.h: Bold's Tim Brooks takes the bass for a 1999 return
years.p: Cappo, Porcelly and Siegler play again as Youth of Today, with [[Tim Brooks|f8e01057-29f6-4be5-968e-4220d6a48ff3]] of [[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]] filling the bass spot.

years.h: Cappo and Porcelly get the rights back and remix We're Not in This Alone
years.p: The third, definitive mix comes out on Revelation in 1997 with new artwork. Rev reissues Can't Close My Eyes the same year.

years.h: Ken Olden of Battery fills in on bass for a European tour
years.p: Cappo, Porcelly and Siegler tour Europe in 2003, with Olden, also of [[Better Than a Thousand|9a5d50be-8dff-4f2f-8852-aa4eafb8f985]], on bass. American shows follow in 2004.

eras.title: Back for good
eras.text: The return that began in Lyss, Switzerland in 2010 never ended. Youth of Today are a working band again, headlining for kids born long after the CBGB matinees, and since 2016 the 1988 rhythm section of Walter Schreifels and Sammy Siegler is back.

years.cap: Youth of Today at the Garage, Saarbrücken, September 17, 2010
years.h: Lyss, Switzerland, is where the comeback starts
years.p: Olden is on bass and Vinny Panza on drums. By the first week of December the band is in Peru, Chile, Argentina and Brazil.

years.cap: Ray Cappo at SO36, Berlin, September 2010
years.h: Moscow, then Oslo
years.p: Two shows in Russia and two in Norway, in March 2011.

years.h: Washington, D.C., on a bill with Mouthpiece and Give
years.p: U Street Music Hall, then the Glasshouse in Pomona and the Chaos in Tejas festival in Austin.

years.h: A full house at This Is Hardcore, Philadelphia
years.p: That October Youth of Today open for [[Danzig|8925a01a-8608-411d-a90b-f3a52d061208]] at Riot Fest in Chicago.

years.cap: Youth of Today at SO36, Berlin, April 28, 2016
years.h: Walter Schreifels and Sammy Siegler rejoin in Berlin
years.p: The 1988 rhythm section plays Berlin that night and Meerhout, Belgium the next.

years.h: Reunion set filmed by hate5six, August 4, 2016
yt: Reunion set filmed by hate5six, August 4, 2016

years.h: Side By Side's final reunion show shares a night with Youth of Today
years.p: Night two of Revelation's festival at 1720 in Los Angeles. [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]] played the night before.
years.xp: Jankysmooth reports that Side By Side played first and Youth of Today closed. Cappo spoke from the stage about "forgetting the many things that divided us and instead focusing on what we all had in common."

years.cap: Youth of Today at The Brooklyn Monarch, November 17, 2022
years.h: Four Northeast nights, with Bold on three of them
years.p: The Met in Pawtucket, The Meadows in Brooklyn, the Lithuanian Music Hall in Philadelphia and Amityville Music Hall, with Swedish Revelation band Speedway on every bill. Thirty-nine years after the two bands first shared a CBGB matinee.
years.xp: Brooklyn Vegan listed Bold on the Brooklyn, Philadelphia and Amityville dates and Speedway on all four. The opening night in Pawtucket had Magnitude, Speedway, Attrition Rites and Just Us.
